display_name: Montes Alpha M, Valle de Colchagua
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Montes Alpha M pulls from Apalta's steep granitic slopes in Colchagua Valley, where alluvial deposits mix with decomposed granite for drainage that stresses vines into concentration. Cool Pacific winds drop nighttime temperatures by 20°C, preserving acidity amid ripening heat. This setup yields a Bordeaux-style blend dense with black fruit and spice.",
  "wine_summary": "Montes Alpha M anchors the producer's push into Chile's luxury tier since 1998, blending Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Carmenère, Merlot, and Petit Verdot from low-yield old vines. Montes, founded by Aurelio Montes and Alfredo Vidaurre, broke from bulk Chilean exports by chasing site-specific quality in Colchagua's subregions. The wine's density comes from Apalta's terroir, where river-transported gravels and granite force deep roots and slow ripening for layered flavor.",
  "terroir_expression": "Colchagua's Teno River lays alluvial loams across the valley floor, but Apalta's amphitheater rises into granitic foothills with quartz veins that shatter into sandy clay. Diurnal swings from coastal fog—days hit 30°C, nights 10°C—build sugars without blowing out acidity, translating to cassis and graphite in the glass from granitic minerality and Carmenère's green pepper pyrazines sharpened by the maritime chill.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested grapes ferment in stainless steel with native yeasts, then age 18 months in 100% new French oak barriques—micro-oxygenation from the wood's tight grain polymerizes tannins for grip without rusticity. Montes sorts rigorously pre-ferment to ditch unripe berries, emphasizing purity. Barrel selection by plot stacks the blend's components for cohesion.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled ribeye with chimichurri: tannins bind steak fats while herbal pyrazines echo the sauce's parsley and garlic. Nashville hot chicken: spice cuts through heat, acidity refreshes fried skin. Lamb shank braised in red wine: slow-cooked collagen melts against structure, earth notes match gamey depth. Cheeseburger with aged cheddar: full body matches beef juiciness, oak vanilla nods to melted cheese.",
  "comparable_wines": "Almaviva Puente Alto — Cabernet-led Chilean blend with similar oak-driven polish and black fruit density. Don Melchor Cabernet Sauvignon — Concha y Toro's Maipo icon matches tannic backbone and aging curve from granitic sites. Seña Aconcagua Valley — Bordeaux varieties blend with Apalta-like concentration and spice.",
  "style_profile": "Cabernet-led full-bodied red with grippy tannins and spicy herbal lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Open 2020 or 2018 now after two hours decant; younger 2023 holds for development. Store at 55°F in darkness, humidity 70%.",
  "value_assessment": "$70-110 retail. Almaviva at $150 and Seña at $120 demand premiums for similar quality. Buy at $80-90—Colchagua blend punches above weight with better freshness than Maipo rivals.",
  "market_position": "High-end steakhouse lists feature it for bold reds under $20/glass. Collectors stock it as Chile's accessible ageworthy pick. Avoid casual retail browsers; suits those trading up from everyday Cabs.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you chase bright Pinot fruit—Alpha M demands food and patience for its savory edge to shine. Blenders like this outpace single-varietal Cabs from Montes at half the price. Underrated Carmenère fraction delivers black pepper thrill missing in straight Bordeaux imports.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 3,
    "tannin": 4,
    "body": 5,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 4,
    "color_intensity": "deep",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "long",
    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "outstanding"
  }
}
